== Problem ==

Jeremy's father drives him to school in rush hour traffic in 20 minutes. One day there is no traffic, so his father can drive him 18 miles per hour faster and gets him to school in 12 minutes. How far in miles is it to school?

<math>
\textbf{(A) } 4 \qquad
\textbf{(B) } 6 \qquad
\textbf{(C) } 8 \qquad
\textbf{(D) } 9 \qquad
\textbf{(E) } 12
</math>


==Solutions==

===Solution 1===

For starters, we identify d as distance and v as velocity (speed)

Writing the equation gives us: <imath>\frac{d}{v}=\frac{1}{3}</imath> and <imath>\frac{d}{v+18}=\frac{1}{5}</imath>.

This gives <imath>d=\frac{1}{5}v+3.6=\frac{1}{3}v</imath>, which gives <imath>v=27</imath>, which then gives <imath>d=\boxed{\textbf{(D)}~9}</imath>.

===Solution 2===
<imath>d = rt</imath>, <imath>d=\frac{1}{3} \times r = \frac{1}{5} \times (r + 18)</imath>

<imath>\frac{r}{3} = \frac{r}{5} + \frac{18}{5}</imath>


<imath>10r = 270</imath> so <imath>r = 27</imath>, plug into the first one and it's <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}~9}</imath> miles to school.

===Solution 3===
We set up an equation in terms of <imath>d</imath> the distance and <imath>x</imath> the speed In miles per hour. We have <imath>d=\left (\dfrac{1}{3}\right )(x)=\left (\dfrac{1}{5}\right) (x+18)</imath>, giving
<cmath>(5)(x)=(3)(x+18)</cmath>
<cmath>5x=3x+54</cmath>
<cmath>2x=54</cmath>
<cmath>x=27</cmath>
Hence, <imath>d=\dfrac{27}{3}=\boxed{\textbf{(D)}~9}</imath>.

===Solution 4===
Since it takes <imath>\frac{3}{5}</imath> of the original time for him to get to school when there is no traffic, the speed must be <imath>\frac{5}{3}</imath> of the speed in no traffic or <imath>\frac{2}{3}</imath> more. Letting <imath>x</imath> be the rate and we know that <imath>\frac{5}{3}x = x + 18</imath>, so we have <imath>\frac{2x}{3} = 18</imath> miles per hour. Solving for <imath>x</imath> gives us <imath>27</imath> miles per hour. Because <imath>20</imath> minutes is a third of an hour, the distance would then be <imath>9</imath> miles <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}~9}</imath>.

===Solution 5===
When driving in rush hour traffic, he drives <imath>20</imath> minutes for one distance (<imath>1d</imath>) to the school. It means he drives <imath>60</imath> minutes for <imath>3</imath> distances (<imath>3d</imath>) to the school. When driving in no traffic hours, he drives <imath>12</imath> minutes for one distance (<imath>1d</imath>) to the school. It means he drives <imath>60</imath> minutes for <imath>5</imath> distances (<imath>5d</imath>) to the school. Subtracting these two situations, it gives us <imath>5d-3d = 18 = 2d</imath>, then <imath>d=\frac{18}{2}=9</imath>. So the distance to the school would be <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}~9}</imath> miles. 
~LarryFlora

===Solution 6===
(Ratios)
<imath>\textbf{requires edits}</imath>

In rush hour traffic, we can create this ratio for each distance we are going to try supposing the distance is <imath>d</imath>:

<imath>d</imath> : <imath>20</imath> hours

In no traffic, we can do the same:

<imath>d</imath> : <imath>12</imath> minutes

We want the ratio to be the distance to <imath>60</imath> minutes:

<imath>d</imath> : <imath>20</imath> minutes = <imath>3</imath>d : <imath>60</imath> minutes 

<imath>d</imath> : <imath>12</imath> minutes = <imath>5</imath>d : <imath>60</imath> minutes

This shows the speed in miles per hour. This means that the speed in the 2nd ratio has to be 18 faster than the first ratio. We get

<imath>3d+18 = 5d \cdot d=9</imath>, or <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}~9}</imath>.

===Solution 7 (Solution 3 but explained better)===

Distance equals speed multiplied by time. Let x/60 represent the speed when Jeremy's father is driving through traffic. Let (x+18)/60 represent the speed when there is no traffic. Because distance equals speed multiplied by time, 20x/60 would represent the distance to school. The "20" in this expression represents the 20 minutes it takes Jeremy's father to drive to school through the traffic, and "60" means 60 minutes. Anyway, 20x/60 simplifies to x/3. Using the same distance equation, the expression 12(x+18)/60 also represents the distance to school. (x+18)/60 represents the speed when there is no traffic, and the "12" means 12 minutes it takes to get to school when there is no traffic. 12(x+18)/60 simplifies to (x+18)/5. Now, since both expressions equate to the distance to school, you get the equation x/3=(x+18)/5. Solving for x gives you 27. This means that Jeremy's father drives 27 miles per hour in traffic. To find the distance to school, simply take 27 and plug it into the expressions (x+18)/5 or x/3. Both give you 9, which is the distance to school.~Evžen D.
